source_read: https://burgerboi.co.uk/allergens/ (the chain's own allergen and nutrition table, heading 'Burger Boi 2026', 'Allergen information last updated 5 October 2026'; my own fetch is byte-identical to the extractor's, sha256 facddd8e26977008e27eab99051c2747ecc31e0af4df7dd0131c58cfd6f1321b) read in headless Chromium (rendered DOM read with my own selectors, then every row expanded and screenshotted: the visible grid of ticks and 'M' marks plus the per-dish 'Nutrition values per serving' panel), cross-checked against the 13 category pages under /menu/ (cards) and the 5 identical /find-your-fuel/*-hub/ marketing pages. robots.txt of burgerboi.co.uk is 'User-agent: * / Allow: /'; 1 request a second, 28 requests in all (script not used).
not_verifiable: serving sizes (the table prints none, so serving is blank); the kJ (not printed); whether the chain's salt figures are right (x6 Tenders 9.2 g, x10 Wings 8.7 g, Hot Mess 6.9 g, Korean Seoul sandwich 6.7 g are high but printed identically in the row and the detail panel and consistent with nothing else on the site to check them against: published as printed); the 41 Halaal marks are the chain's own words and nothing else on its site says what 'Halaal' means for its supply.
notes: SAMPLE: all 39 dishes the extractor published (fewer than 40, so every one), field by field: calories, protein, carbs, fat, saturates, sugars, fibre and salt (8 figures), the 14 allergen cells (Contains / May contain), the named cereal (wheat) and tree-nut handling, the Vegetarian/Vegan marks, the vegetarian tag, the category and name; 663 comparisons against items.csv + allergens.csv and 385 more against the built chain JSON (35 published items): 0 mismatches. The title tag '(NNN kcal)', the hidden table cells and the expanded detail panel agree for every dish. The classification of the other 38 dishes was redone from my own read: 4 print kcal/carbs/protein with no fat (the Fuel dishes), 11 print protein only, 23 print nothing (the whole Manchester breakfast menu among them): exactly the extractor's counts, so nothing publishable was left out. Energy check 4P+4C+9F within 8% for all 39, saturates <= fat and sugars <= carbs everywhere. Every allergen row was also compared by eye on a screenshot of the rendered grid (10 contact sheets, 39 dishes): all agree. Where a dish names wheat as contained and barley/oats/rye as may-contain, the extractor publishes generic gluten (policy 2 of docs/ACCURACY_AUDIT.md); I re-derived that for all 39 and it holds. Menu-page cards (13 pages, 70 cards): every protein/carb/kcal figure on a card equals the table's except American (table 35.0 g, card 34g) and Hot Honey smash burger (table 42.0 g, card 41g), already held back by the extractor; the sauces page's 'Korean Seoul' card is a verbatim copy of the chicken sandwich card (33g) and is not a figure for the sauce (table 1.1 g). TWO CHAIN SELF-CONTRADICTIONS THE EXTRACTOR HAD NOT HELD BACK, now held back in tools/uk_extract/burger_boi.py (so a re-run reproduces them; check_chain 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 high and 0 medium audit flags, 35 items shown): (1) Ranch: the table marks it 'Suitable for Vegetarian, Vegan, Halaal' and also 'Contains: Eggs, Milk', which cannot both be true (the only such row of the 77); no vegan claim is published, but the row rests on a contradiction, so held back as the project does for vegan dishes marked milk or egg. (2) Triple Cheese: the five identical 'Find your fuel' hub pages (found by me; the extractor had read 16 pages but not these) print 'Triple Cheese Boi' with the same beef, American cheese, lettuce, pickles, cheese sauce and signature sauce at 61g protein, against 55.0 g in the table and on the /menu/smashed-burgers/ card. Same rule the extractor applied to American and Hot Honey for a 1 g gap; here the gap is 11%. The hub also gives Hot Honey Smash 54g (table 42.0, card 41g), Cali Peri Bowl 48g/540 cal (table 39.0/382 kcal, card 39g/382 kcal), Teriyaki Beef Bowl 47g/520 cal (table 32.0/514, card 32g/514), and lists a Korean Seoul Bowl and a Caesar Wrap that are not in the table at all; the last four are unpublished or already held. The hub is weak evidence (one templated marketing page printed five times, it names Bristol though the sitemap has no Bristol shop, calls the 61g dish the highest-protein item although the table prints 66 g for the half chicken and 77 g for ten wings, and shows a 'SEARCH.NO' placeholder), so holding Triple Cheese is a judgement, not a proof: delete its line in data/source/burger-boi/holdback.csv to publish it on the table and card, which agree at 55 g. HUB_ALIASES in the script maps 'Triple Cheese Boi' and 'Hot Honey Smash' to the table's dishes. Because Triple Cheese is no longer published, the halal quote (data/dietary/halal-burger-boi.csv, regenerated by the script) now cites Jamin (782 kcal) instead of Triple Cheese; the 41-of-77 Halaal ticks (39 of them on dishes with full nutrition) were verified in cells, detail lines and screenshots. MARKED OK: Chipotle Mayo (audit 'name-implies-eggs'): the table marks it Vegan with no egg even as may-contain, and the Korean Seoul sandwich and Halloumi Burger, whose cards name chipotle mayo, mark no egg either, so the egg-free row is consistent (data/audit/reviewed/burger-boi.csv). Noted only, left published: the Korean Seoul sandwich marks milk as may-contain while Bird Boi and the Hot Honey sandwich mark it contained (no ingredient text names milk or buttermilk on the site; 'buttermilk' appears only in the page's address, and the allergy filters hide a may-contain dish too); Garlic & Herb 537 kcal and Southern Gravy 3 kcal show the serving sizes are unknown; the innocent smoothies carry no Vegetarian mark so get no tag.
